eli5: A computer that is always on and always connected, so other people can visit the website or app that lives on it. It is often a rented computer you never see.
english: A computer that runs your website or apps around the clock. Usually rented from a hosting company, sometimes a small box at home.
dev: A machine (VPS, dedicated host, home server) running your services. infra-guardian never connects to it by itself; it only guides the changes Claude makes.

eli5: Running your own website or apps on a computer you control, instead of using a company's ready-made version.
english: Running tools such as WordPress or a CRM yourself, on a server you control, instead of paying a company to run them for you.
dev: Operating services on infrastructure you administer yourself (VPS, home server) instead of consuming SaaS.

eli5: A folder of instructions that Claude reads, so it behaves in a certain careful way for a certain kind of job. Like a recipe card Claude keeps in its pocket.
english: A packaged set of instructions (and sometimes small scripts) that Claude loads when your request matches it. This one makes Claude careful around your servers.
dev: A SKILL.md with a name and a description that decides when it triggers, plus supporting files. Here SKILL.md holds ten rules, and scripts/ holds four Python helpers.

eli5: A spare copy of a file, made before you change it, so you can put it back the way it was.
english: A saved copy of a file taken before a change. In this tool it only counts once it has been checked against the original.
dev: A copy made by scripts/backup.py with shutil.copy2, kept only after its SHA-256 matches the source, and recorded in state.json.

eli5: Putting the saved copy back where the changed file is, so things go back to how they were.
english: Putting a backup back in place of the current file. The current file is saved first, so a restore can itself be undone.
dev: backup.py --restore ID or --restore-last. It re-verifies the stored copy, writes NAME.pre-restore.STAMP beside the live file, copies, then verifies again.

eli5: A fingerprint for a file. If two files have the same fingerprint, they are exactly the same.
english: A short code worked out from a file's contents. If the copy and the original give the same code, the copy is perfect.
dev: SHA-256 hex digest computed in 64 KiB chunks and compared between source and copy.

eli5: The name of one particular fingerprint recipe for files.
english: The method this tool uses to make a file's checksum. Change one letter in the file and the code changes completely.
dev: hashlib.sha256 over the file bytes.

eli5: Practising without really doing it. It tells you what would happen and changes nothing.
english: A preview that shows what would happen without changing anything.
dev: The --dry-run flag on backup.py. It prints BACK UP or SKIP and the reason, and returns before any backup, session or state is written.

eli5: A hidden file where secret passwords for other services are kept, so they are not written in the open.
english: A hidden file in the project folder that holds secret keys. It is listed in .gitignore, so it is never uploaded.
dev: Plain KEY=value lines. infra-status-check.py reads it with its own minimal parser (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID). Gitignored.

eli5: A long secret code that proves to another service that you are allowed to use it, like a library card.
english: A password-like code from another service that lets a tool use that service on your behalf. Keep it private.
dev: Provider credentials listed as placeholders in .env.example (Mistral, NVIDIA, Groq, Cerebras, OpenRouter, Gemini). No script in the repo reads them.

eli5: A way of writing settings as a plain list in a text file.
english: A plain text format for settings files. Indentation matters, so the spaces at the start of a line are part of the meaning.
dev: Parsed with PyYAML safe_load. Duplicate top-level keys are accepted and the last one wins, which is what guardian.config.example.yaml relies on by accident.

eli5: The settings file. It tells the helper how you like things done.
english: The settings file, guardian.config.yaml. Made from the example file, and never uploaded.
dev: guardian.config.yaml, looked up by backup.py as --config, then the current folder, then ~/.infra-guardian/. doctor.py and setup.py use the repo root only.

eli5: A second copy of your backup kept somewhere else, in case the first place breaks.
english: An optional second place that gets a copy of each backup, ideally on a different disk.
dev: Optional backup.mirror path in the config. The copy is verified by SHA-256 too; a failed mirror only warns, it does not fail the backup.

eli5: Making your own copy of a project from the internet onto your computer.
english: Downloading a project's whole folder from GitHub with git, so you have it on your own computer.
dev: git clone https://github.com/Stravelakis/infra-guardian.git. The v0.3 release has no attached download, so cloning is the install.

eli5: A window where you type a command and press Enter, instead of clicking.
english: The text window where you type commands. On Windows it is PowerShell or Command Prompt; on Mac it is the Terminal app.
dev: Any shell. The docs show python3; on Windows the same scripts run with python.

eli5: A programming language. You do not need to learn it, only to have it installed so the little helper scripts can run.
english: The language the four helper scripts are written in. You need it installed, but you never have to write any.
dev: Python 3. The code calls Path.unlink(missing_ok=True), so 3.8 or newer in practice.

eli5: A small add-on that lets Python read settings files.
english: A small add-on for Python that reads the settings file. Install it with pip install pyyaml.
dev: Imported at the top of backup.py and infra-status-check.py. Without it both exit with a plain message (backup.py exits 2).

eli5: A chat app. The helper can send you a short message there, if you set it up.
english: A chat app. The optional self-check can send you its A/B/C suggestions through a Telegram bot you create.
dev: infra-status-check.py posts to the Bot API sendMessage endpoint with urllib, only if telegram.enabled is true and both .env values are set.

eli5: An alarm clock for a computer. It starts a job at set times.
english: A schedule that runs the self-check by itself. On Linux that is a systemd user timer you set up yourself.
dev: doctor.py looks for systemctl --user is-enabled infra-status-check.timer. No unit file ships in the repo.

eli5: When things have slowly changed so they no longer match what you wrote down.
english: When the real setup no longer matches your notes about it.
dev: In infra-status-check.py, only a text check on status.md (open items, missing "Verified?" column). It does not probe any server.

eli5: A grown-up job: the person who looks after servers so they keep working.
english: A system administrator, someone whose job is running servers. This tool is for people who are not one.
dev: The skill's target user is the opposite: a non-coder who self-hosts.

eli5: The internet's phone book. It turns a name like example.com into the address of a computer.
english: The system that turns a domain name into a server address. One of the things the reference library explains.
dev: Covered by references/providers/dns.md. A change here is one of the "touches DNS" triggers in the skill description.

eli5: A tool that remembers the people and companies you deal with.
english: Customer relationship manager: software that keeps track of your contacts. The library has a note on Twenty CRM.
dev: references/selfhosted/twenty-crm.md.

eli5: A popular tool for building websites without writing code.
english: A very popular website builder. The library has notes on WordPress itself, its database, hosting and eight plugins.
dev: references/wordpress/ (wordpress.md, database.md, _hosting.md, plugins.md) and references/wordpress/plugins/ (eight plugin notes).
